question: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Nikolas Farantouris (S&D) Subject:

On 30 June, the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy visited Ankara together with the Commissioner for Enlargement and the Commissioner for Migration and Home Affairs. The meeting was followed by a joint press release issued together with the Turkish Foreign Minister. The press release underlines the ‘strategic value’ of EU-Türkiye relations in promoting regional stability, security and economic resilience1. However, there is no mention of Türkiye persistent attempts to undermine the sovereign rights and legitimate interests of EU Member States, such as challenging the maritime zones of Greece and Cyprus, preparing the upcoming ‘Blue Homeland’ law, obstructing the European project to connect the power grids of Greece and Cyprus and excluding Cyprus from the COP31 meetings. In view of the above, can the Vice-President / High Representative answer the following: 1.

Did she, during the meeting with the Turkish leadership, raise the issues of the casus belli, the challenges to the sovereign rights of Greece and Cyprus, the Kasos incident, and Türkiye’s ongoing revisionist policy ?

How does the recognition of Türkiye as a strategic partner square with the persistent challenges to the sovereign rights of Member States and what specific conditions does the EU intend to lay down to make the further deepening of EU-Türkiye relations conditional on full respect for international law and the good neighbourliness principle2?
Can EU foreign policy be decoupled from full respect for the sovereign rights of EU Member States?

https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_26_1495 It should be noted that in a recent answer she gave, the Vice-President / High Representative underlined the unwavering commitment to defending the sovereign rights and interests of the Member States and the need for Türkiye to fully respect international law, the Law of the Sea and good neighbourly relations (https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/E-10-2026-002001-ASW_EN.html). 1 2
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.8.2026) The EU remains committed to defending its interests and those of its Member States, as well as to upholding regional stability. The sovereignty and sovereign rights of all EU Member States must be respected. In this context, the EU has consistently underlined that Türkiye is expected to make an unequivocal commitment to good neighbourly relations, international agreements and the peaceful settlement of disputes, in accordance with international law and the UN Charter. The EU continues to follow developments in the Aegean and the Eastern Mediterranean closely and will raise matters of concern with Türkiye through the appropriate channels. An unequivocal commitment to international law, including the Law of the Sea, international agreements and the UN Charter, remains essential, as does abstaining from unilateral actions which violate international law and the sovereign rights of Member States. These are essential requirements to ensure a stable and secure environment in the Eastern Mediterranean and the development of a cooperative and mutually beneficial relationship between the EU and Türkiye. As stated in the joint press release1 issued following the visit to Ankara on 30 June 2026, the EU and Türkiye acknowledged the strategic value of their relationship in promoting regional stability, security and economic resilience. They also reaffirmed the shared determination to take steps that would further enhance the cooperative and mutually beneficial relationship and agreed on the importance of regional stability and good neighbourly relations. At the same time, such engagement continues to be based on the relevant European Council conclusions, including the need for sustained de-escalation and a constructive approach by Türkiye.
